bug_description.original: Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5638857115041792 Project: open62541 Fuzzer: afl_open62541_fuzz_binary_decode Fuzz target binary: fuzz_binary_decode Job Type: afl_asan_open62541 Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ 4 Crash Address: 0x610000000350 Crash State: DataValue_clear clear_noInit DataValue_clear Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Recommended Security Severity: High Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=afl_asan_open62541&range=201811160414:201811180356 Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=5638857115041792 Issue filed automatically.
bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 11484: open62541 has a heap-use-after-free (READ of size 4) in the OPC UA type deep-copy/clear machinery. Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ 4. Crash State: Variant_clear / clear_noInit / UA_clear. Sanitizer: address (ASAN). The fuzz target fuzz_binary_decode decodes a UA value from untrusted bytes and then UA_copy-deep-copies it; a failed copy under an artificial allocation limit runs cleanup that frees a Variant's data array without nulling the pointer, so a second clear re-reads the freed Variant.

source.code: UA_StatusCode ret = UA_decodeBinary(&binary, newOffset, dst, &UA_TYPES[typeIndex], NULL);
source.description: The untrusted fuzzer bytes are parsed by the OPC UA binary decoder into a live typed object `dst` (a nested UA_Variant/UA_DataValue holding attacker-shaped array lengths and elements). This project decode/materialization point is the scored source; the decoded structure is what is later deep-copied and cleaned up, triggering the UAF.
source.value_from: untrusted OPC UA binary-encoded bytes from the fuzzer input; value `dst` decoded via `UA_decodeBinary(&binary, newOffset, dst, &UA_TYPES[typeIndex], NULL)` where `binary` wraps the input buffer.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer reports a heap-use-after-free READ of size 4 here: Variant_clear reads the `storageType` field of a UA_Variant that lives inside an array region already freed by an earlier cleanup pass. It is reached by a second traversal (UA_clear -> clear_noInit -> Variant_clear) over the same dangling `data` pointer.

root_cause.description: Variant_clear frees the variant's data array via UA_Array_delete but does not reset `p->data = NULL` afterwards. The variant object retains a dangling pointer, so when the same (or an aliasing) variant is cleared a second time during error cleanup, the guard `p->data > UA_EMPTY_ARRAY_SENTINEL` still passes and the freed array is re-traversed and read. The fix commit adds `p->data = NULL;` immediately after this call.

tainted_value_origin.description: During the deep copy of the decoded variant, UA_Array_copy allocates the element array (`*dst`, the 192-byte region that ASan later reports) sized from the attacker-controlled `size`/arrayLength. This array is assigned into the destination variant's `data`; it is the object that is subsequently freed by cleanup and then read-after-free.

parser_admitted.description: The input selected a valid UA_TYPES index and was successfully decoded by UA_decodeBinary (ret == UA_STATUSCODE_GOOD), so execution is admitted into the deep-copy path (UA_copy at line 38) that reaches the vulnerable clear machinery.

coarse_trace.summary: Deep-copies the freshly decoded typed value via UA_copy(dst, dstCopy, type).
Generic copy entry; zero-inits dst then calls copy_noInit.
Per-member copy dispatch through copyJumpTable into DataValue_copy.
memcpy(dst,src) then Variant_copy of the value member.
Copies the variant's element array via UA_Array_copy.
Allocates the element array and copies each element; a nested copy fails under the memory limit, driving cleanup.
On the failed element copy, UA_clear(dst) is invoked to clean up the partial element.
Clear dispatch through clearJumpTable into Variant_clear for the element.
Frees the variant's data array via UA_Array_delete without nulling p->data.
Iterates the (dangling) array clearing each element via UA_clear.
Reads p->storageType of a freed variant element -> heap-use-after-free READ 4.

fine_trace.code: UA_StatusCode ret = UA_decodeBinary(&binary, newOffset, dst, &UA_TYPES[typeIndex], NULL);
fine_trace.note: Source: untrusted bytes are decoded into a live nested UA_Variant/UA_DataValue whose array lengths and elements are attacker-shaped.
The admitted decoded object enters the generic deep-copy that exercises the vulnerable copy/clear machinery.
Member-wise copy dispatch routes into DataValue_copy for the value member.

DataValue_copy bulk-copies all of src's fields into dst, so dst transiently aliases src's nested variant/data pointers before the value is re-initialized and re-copied. This aliasing is why a single freed array becomes reachable from two cleanup traversals.
The variant's element array is deep-copied; length/src->data come from the attacker-decoded structure.
Allocates the element array region (the 192-byte block ASan reports at 0x610000000340). This is the object later freed and then read-after-free.

Element-by-element copy loop; the custom memory manager's last-4-bytes limit makes a nested UA_calloc return NULL, so an element copy fails and its cleanup path (UA_copy -> UA_clear at line 960) begins while the parent copy is still unwinding.

ROOT CAUSE: the first cleanup pass frees the variant's data array here but never sets p->data = NULL (the fix adds `p->data = NULL;` right after). The variant object is left holding a dangling pointer.
The array region is freed. Because p->data was not reset in the caller, the freed address remains stored in the variant.
A second cleanup traversal reaches the same (aliased) dangling array and iterates its elements, dereferencing freed memory to clear each element variant.

SINK: Variant_clear reads storageType of a variant element inside the freed region -> heap-use-after-free READ of size 4. Why-crash edges: order = the array was freed at step 9 before this read (free_before_use); control = the un-nulled p->data kept the guard `p->data > UA_EMPTY_ARRAY_SENTINEL` true so this second clear re-entered the freed structure; data = the read targets the freed region reachable via the dangling p.

format.name: OPC UA binary-encoded value (open62541 fuzz_binary_decode input)
format.contract: Candidate input must keep the leading 2-byte type index selecting a UA_TYPES entry whose decoded value is a nested variant/array, remain decodable by UA_decodeBinary (parser-admitted, ret == UA_STATUSCODE_GOOD), and preserve the trailing 4-byte allocation-limit word so that a UA_calloc during the subsequent UA_copy fails mid-way. That forced copy failure drives the Variant_clear cleanup path that frees an un-nulled variant data array and re-reads it (heap-use-after-free in Variant_clear).
